# Quality Control Templates

![_Templates.  Jewelry Templates. Quality Control Templates. AP | Pivtorak.Studio. 30.10.2026_ © Anna Pivtorak (Kostyuk)](/images/templates-jewelry-templates-quality-control-templates.webp)

Quality Control Templates present a selection of simplified inspection forms and checklists used to document the condition, dimensions, workmanship, and overall quality of finished jewelry. These materials introduce the basic principles of quality assessment and help students understand how a jewelry piece is examined at different stages of its creation. They demonstrate how observations, measurements, identified defects, and inspection results can be recorded in a structured and consistent way.

The templates are designed primarily for educational purposes, particularly for students of art history who wish to understand the relationship between jewelry design, technical documentation, and the evaluation of a finished object. They provide an accessible introduction to the terminology and structure of quality control records without replacing professional manufacturing documentation.

## Dimensional Inspection Sheet

A simplified inspection form for recording and comparing the principal dimensions of a jewelry piece with the measurements indicated in its technical drawing.

The sheet helps students understand how dimensional accuracy is assessed and how measured values are documented.

Typical fields include:
- Jewelry Piece Identification
- Reference Drawing or Design
- Dimension Description
- Specified Measurement
- Actual Measurement
- Inspection Result
- Notes and Observations

## Finished Jewelry Inspection Checklist

A checklist for examining the general condition and visible quality of a completed jewelry piece. It introduces the main aspects considered during a visual inspection of finished jewelry.

The checklist helps students recognize the relationship between design intentions, workmanship, surface treatment, and the appearance of the final object.

Typical inspection points include:
- Overall Appearance and Condition
- Surface Finish and Polishing
- Joints and Connections
- Setting and Stone Security
- Moving or Functional Elements
- Visible Imperfections
- General Inspection Result

## Defect Identification and Rework Record

A simplified record for documenting visible defects or imperfections identified during the inspection of a jewelry piece, together with any proposed corrective actions.

It helps students understand how defects are described, located, and recorded, and how corrections can be documented for reference.

Typical fields include:
- Jewelry Piece Identification
- Defect Location
- Defect Description
- Visual Reference or Sketch
- Proposed Corrective Action
- Rework Status
- Additional Notes

## Final Product Approval Sheet

A summary form for recording the final inspection and approval status of a completed jewelry piece. It brings together the main observations made during the quality assessment process.

The sheet helps students understand how the completed object is compared with its approved design and how the final inspection outcome is documented.

Typical fields include:
- Jewelry Piece Identification
- Approved Design Reference
- Overall Condition
- Design and Drawing Conformity
- Inspection Summary
- Final Approval Status
- Comments and Confirmation

## Quality Inspection Record by Production Stage

A simplified record for documenting quality checks at different stages of jewelry production. It demonstrates that inspection is not limited to the completed object but can also take place throughout the creation process.

The record helps students understand how the condition and quality of a jewelry piece can be evaluated progressively, from an individual manufacturing stage to the final result.

Typical fields include:
- Production Stage
- Component or Area Inspected
- Inspection Criteria
- Observed Condition
- Inspection Result
- Notes and Observations
